questions.q: A metal rod is divided into three parts A, B and C. The lengths of A and B are in the ratio 9 : 20, and the lengths of C and B are in the ratio 5 : 11. If the difference between the lengths of A and C is 10 cm, find the total length (in cm) of the metal rod.
questions.solution:
A : B = 9 : 20 and B : C = 11 : 5, so A : B : C = 99 : 220 : 100.
A and C differ by $100 - 99 = 1$ unit, and 1 unit = 10 cm, so total $= 419 \times 10 = 4190$ cm.
**Answer: 4190**
questions.shortcut: Equate B first: A:B:C = 99:220:100; the 1-unit gap between A and C is the given 10 cm.

questions.q: Soniya got married 15 years ago. Her present age is 8/5 times her age at the time of her marriage. Her sister was 8 years younger to her at the time of her marriage. Find the present age of her sister.
questions.solution:
Let Soniya's age at marriage be $x$: $x + 15 = \frac{8x}{5}$, so $x = 25$.
She is 40 now, so her sister was $25 - 8 = 17$ at the marriage and is $17 + 15 = 32$ now.
**Answer: 32 years**
questions.shortcut: Her age grew by 3/5 of itself in 15 years, so marriage age = 25; sister = 25 − 8 + 15.

questions.q: The average age of 26 students of a class is 26 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 27 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
Total age of 26 students $= 26 \times 26 = 676$ years.
With the teacher, total $= 27 \times 27 = 729$ years, so the teacher is $729 - 676 = 53$ years old.
**Answer: 53**

questions.q: If $\Delta \times 2.2 + 0.33 \times \frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{20} \times 0.55 = 0.99$, then the value of $\Delta$ is:
Smriti goes to a shopping mall at a speed of 21 km/hr and returns at a speed of 69 km/hr. Find her average speed (in km/hr) for the entire trip.
questions.solution:
For equal distances, average speed $= \frac{2xy}{x+y} = \frac{2 \times 21 \times 69}{21 + 69} = \frac{2898}{90} = 32.2$ km/hr.
**Answer: 32.2**
questions.shortcut: Two equal legs: use 2ab/(a+b), never the simple mean of 21 and 69.

questions.q: An article was bought for ₹8,900. Its price was marked up by 40%. Thereafter, it was sold at a discount of 5% on the marked price. What was the profit percentage on the transaction?
questions.solution:
Marked price $= 8900 \times 1.40 = 12460$ and selling price $= 12460 \times 0.95 = 11837$.
Profit $= 2937$, i.e. $\frac{2937}{8900} \times 100 = 33\%$.
**Answer: 33%**
questions.shortcut: Net factor = 1.40 × 0.95 = 1.33 → profit 33% in one step.

questions.q: Which of the following ratios is equivalent to 3 : 2?
questions.solution:
An equivalent ratio has both terms multiplied by the same number.
$54 = 3 \times 18$ and $36 = 2 \times 18$, so 54 : 36 = 3 : 2.
**Answer: 54 : 36**

questions.q: If tan θ = 12/5, what is the value of sec θ?
questions.solution:
Take opposite = 12 and adjacent = 5, so hypotenuse $= \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = 13$.
$\sec\theta = \frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{13}{5}$.
**Answer: 13/5**

questions.q: Two numbers have an HCF of 18 and an LCM of 1512. If one of the numbers is 126, find the positive difference between these numbers.
questions.solution:
Product of the numbers $= \text{HCF} \times \text{LCM} = 18 \times 1512 = 27216$.
Second number $= \frac{27216}{126} = 216$, so the difference $= 216 - 126 = 90$.
**Answer: 90**

questions.q: Out of 100, the marks of 21 students in a final exam are 90, 95, 95, 94, 90, 85, 84, 83, 85, 81, 92, 93, 82, 78, 79, 81, 80, 82, 85, 76, 85. The mode of the data is:
questions.solution:
The value 85 appears four times, more than any other mark (95 and 90 appear only twice).
So the mode is 85.
**Answer: 85**
questions.shortcut: Mode = most frequent value; 85 repeats four times.

questions.q: A fruit vendor bought 150 mangoes. He sold them at such a price that the selling price of 120 mangoes equals the cost price of 150 mangoes. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Let the cost of one mango be ₹1, so the cost of 150 mangoes is ₹150, which equals the selling price of 120 mangoes.
Selling price of one mango $= \frac{150}{120} = 1.25$, i.e. 25% above cost.
**Answer: 25%**

questions.q: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 40 minutes, 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, and they discharge chemical solutions P, Q and R. With all three opened on an empty tank, what is the proportion of solution Q in the liquid in the tank after 9 minutes?
questions.solution:
In 9 minutes the parts filled by A, B, C are $\frac{9}{40}, \frac{9}{20}, \frac{9}{30}$, so the share of Q is $\frac{9/20}{9/40 + 9/20 + 9/30}$.
Using 120 as the common denominator: $\frac{6}{3 + 6 + 4} = \frac{6}{13}$.
**Answer: 6/13**
questions.shortcut: Compare filling rates 1/40 : 1/20 : 1/30 = 3 : 6 : 4, so Q = 6/13 of the tank.

questions.q: Two-fifth of a container is filled with blue liquid, one-third of the remaining is filled with black liquid, five-sixth of the still-remaining part is filled with yellow liquid, and the remaining 4.2 litres holds white liquid. Find the total capacity of the container.
questions.solution:
After blue, $\frac{3}{5}$ remains; black takes $\frac{1}{3}$ of that, leaving $\frac{2}{5}$; yellow takes $\frac{5}{6}$ of that, leaving $\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{15}$ of the tank.
So $\frac{T}{15} = 4.2$, giving $T = 63$ litres.
**Answer: 63 litres**

$1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{30}{24}$, so the braces give $\frac{1}{24}$, and $\frac{13}{4} \div \frac{1}{24} = 78$.
Then $5 \times \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{3}$ and $78 \div \frac{1}{3} = 234$.
**Answer: 234**

questions.q: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 6 days. B alone can do the same work in 12 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
questions.solution:
A's one-day rate $= \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{12}$, so A alone needs 12 days for one job.
Double the work takes $12 \times 2 = 24$ days.
**Answer: 24**
questions.shortcut: A's time = (6 × 12)/(12 − 6) = 12 days for one job; double it.

questions.q: A scheme like 'Buy 6, Get 4 Free' on articles of the same kind with the same MRP attracts a discount of what per cent?
questions.solution:
The customer pays the MRP of 6 articles but receives 10.
Discount $= \frac{4}{10} \times 100 = 40\%$ on the total value received.
**Answer: 40**

questions.q: The amount on a sum of ₹6,800 at 15% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years' time, will be:
